title: Daily GPU slice decomposition - APAC/EU/NA snapshot 2026-03-20
body:
Purpose:
Quick daily export & decomposition of GPU utilization (slices) across APAC, EU, and NA clusters. This is a lightweight snapshot intended for ops triage and short-horizon capacity decisions; not final monthly capacity plan.

Data sources & notes:
- Dashboard export: internal dashboard 'gpu-slices-v2' (time window: 2026-03-19 00:00 -> 2026-03-19 23:59 UTC).
- Aggregation: per-cluster metrics rolled up to pool-level by affinity tag (latency-critical, batch, preemptable, training).
- Metrics included: avg_util, p95_util, p99_util, sustained90m (percent of 90-minute windows >90%), avg_queue_depth, cache_prefix_hit_rate.
- Sampling cadence: 1m -> rolled to 5m for sheet.
- Known caveat: APAC metric agent had a delayed heartbeat 2026-03-19 14:00-14:10 UTC; short gap interpolated.

Topline fleet numbers (2026-03-19 UTC):
- Fleet total GPUs (prod-facing): 8,520 GPUs
- Regional split: NA 3,820 | EU 2,350 | APAC 2,350
- Fleet average utilization (weighted by GPUs): 61.3%
- Fleet p95 utilization: 93.8% (short tails driven by NA latency pools)

Pool decomposition (weighted by GPU count):
- latency-critical (vCPU pin, small-batch): 28% of GPUs; avg_util 69%; p95 98%; sustained90m 14%
- batch (elastic jobs, flexible scheduling): 34% of GPUs; avg_util 47%; p95 72%; sustained90m 2%
- preemptable (spot / burst): 22% of GPUs; avg_util 58%; p95 81%; sustained90m 6%
- training (long jobs, >4h): 16% of GPUs; avg_util 52%; p95 77%; sustained90m 9%

Region + cluster exceptions called out:
- APAC (region-wide): avg_util 67%, p95 97% — highest contention midday. Root cause: coordinated e2e load test + two latency-critical pools from partner onboarding (rollout INFRA-1162). See JIRA INFRA-1162 for rollout plan.
- NA cluster-c49: sustained90m = 46% (sustained high). Cluster c49 hosts many small latency-critical models (mix of 7B and 13B). IOPS spikes correlate with prefix cache cold misses; cache_prefix_hit_rate dropped to 31% during the spike window.
- EU cluster-e18: observed sustained batch ramp 18:00-22:00 UTC; queue_depth peaked 420 jobs queued for batch queue 'mage-batch-v2'. Autoscale min_replicas incorrectly set to 8 (should be 16) in cluster config (PR referenced).

Headroom & immediate risk assessment (short horizon, next 72h):
- Overall buffer (naive): ~3,300 GPUs free at baseline average (if shifting all pools evenly).
- Effective headroom for latency-critical (without preemption): ~420 GPUs across regions (conservative: assume re-reserving 10% of batch & preemptable).
- At current growth (observed 7-day rolling increase +5.1% GPU-minutes/day), APAC may hit latency SLO risk within 48-72h for latency-critical pool unless we:
   * throttle non-critical batch jobs OR
   * move 120 GPUs of dedicated latency capacity from NA->APAC (cross-region migration plan exists but risk: live traffic DNS flapping).

Suggested mitigations (short checklist):
- [ ] Throttle batch fair-share in APAC for next 36h (owner: Marco H) - throttle policy: cap per-tenant batch concurrency by 20%
- [ ] Push autoscale fix on cluster-e18 (owner: Liang W) - PR #910 is ready to land; needs canary testing in eu-west-2 staging
- [ ] Enable prefix warmup for c49 latency pool (owner: Aisha P) - prefetch top-500 prefixes for 2x warmup window at 02:00 UTC nightly
- [ ] Run small cross-region migration of 24 GPUs to APAC (owner: SRE oncall) as a canary to validate migration scripts

Short CSV-style excerpt (cluster-level 24h rollup) - columns: date,cluster,region,pool,gpus,avg_util,p95,sustained90m,queue_avg,cache_prefix_hit

Anomaly deep-dive notes (brief):
- c49 spike window 2026-03-19 13:40-14:20 UTC: tail latency jump matched a set of ~30k requests that had longer prefix lengths; likely model prompting variation. Data science team flagged a daily-data pipeline test at ~13:30 UTC. Recommend correlate with DS pipeline logs (ticket: JIRA-DS-2209).
- cache_prefix_hit_rate falls to mid-30s when many small requests bypass the warm cache; this is the main lever to bring down p95 in latency pools.

Forecasting quick back-of-envelope (48h):
- If APAC growth continues at current 7-day daily delta +5% and no mitigations: latency-critical headroom will be exhausted in ~2.1 days.
- If throttle batch by 20% in APAC: buys ~1.3 days.
- If move 120 GPUs from NA -> APAC (cold migration, 6h ops window): buys ~2.7 days but carries cross-region risk.

Operational asks / next steps:
1) Approve temporary batch throttle policy for APAC (Marco) - target decision within 2h.
2) Land autoscale fix (PR #910) and canary to eu-west-2 tonight (Liang) - ETA 8h.
3) Schedule prefix-warmup cron for c49 (Aisha) - low-risk, ETA 24h.
4) If the above insufficient, prepare cross-region 120 GPU migration playbook (SRE runbook reference in linked artifacts).

Slack threads & references:
- #infra-apac (thread: \"apac-midday-surge-19mar\")
- #sre-oncall (thread: \"c49-tail-latency\")

Appendix: metric definitions (short)
- avg_util: time-weighted average GPU compute utilization (0-100).
- p95/p99: percentile utilization across 5m samples in window.
- sustained90m: percent of contiguous 90-minute windows where avg_util >90%.
- queue_avg: average job queue length for the pool (jobs).
- cache_prefix_hit_rate: fraction of requests served from prefix/KV cache (0-100).

Notes on uniqueness: this sheet focuses on 'slice decomposition' language (pool-by-affinity breakdown + prefix cache behavior) and cross-region immediate action suggestions rather than full monthly capacity forecasts. It's intentionally concise for ops decision-making.

If you want, I can:
- drop a 7-day timeseries export per-cluster as a CSV in this doc,
- run a simulated throttle impact model to quantify expected drop in p95, or
- expand the migration playbook with step-by-step commands.

-- Aisha
